prompt: Describe your typical morning routine and say what you would like to change.
goals: use the present simple for routines
order events with first / then / after that
use I'd like to + verb
model: I usually wake up at six thirty. First, I make coffee and check my messages. Then I take a shower and get dressed. After that, I have breakfast and leave for work at eight. Because the traffic is bad, I often arrive tired. I'd like to wake up earlier and exercise for twenty minutes, since it would give me more energy for the whole day.

prompt: Tell me about a trip you really enjoyed. Where did you go, and what did you do?
goals: use the past simple
order events with first / then / finally
give a reason with because
model: Last year, I went to Salvador with my sister. We stayed in a small hostel near the beach. First, we visited the old town, and then we tried local food like acarajé. The best part was the music in the streets at night. Finally, we took a boat trip, which was amazing because the water was so clear. I'd love to go back someday.

prompt: Describe a good friend and explain why you get along so well.
goals: use the present simple
give reasons with because
use a relative clause with who or which
model: My best friend is Rafael. We met at university, and we've been friends for ten years. We get along because we have the same sense of humor, and he always listens when I have a problem. He's also very honest, which I really appreciate. Even though we live in different cities now, we talk every week.

prompt: How do you use your phone every day? Is it useful, distracting, or both?
goals: use the present simple with frequency adverbs
use one contrast connector: however / but
give a reason with because
model: I use my phone all day. In the morning, I check the news and my messages. At work, I use it to join calls and answer emails. It's very useful. However, it can also be distracting, especially when I get notifications from social media. Because of that, I usually turn off notifications in the evening, so I can relax and sleep better.

prompt: Describe a traditional festival or dish from your country.
goals: use the present simple to describe traditions
use usually and often
give an example with for example
model: A famous tradition in Brazil is the Festa Junina. It usually takes place in June, and people often wear colorful clothes and dance in groups. There's a lot of special food, for example, corn cake and sweet rice pudding. I like it because everyone, from children to grandparents, enjoys it together. It's also a great opportunity to spend time with family.

prompt: Describe your job or your studies. What do you like and what don't you like about it?
goals: use the present simple
contrast with on the other hand
give reasons with because or since
useful: On the other hand, I don't like...
model: I work as a systems analyst for a medium-sized company. I like my job because I solve problems every day and I learn something new all the time. The team is also very friendly. On the other hand, I don't like having too many meetings, since they take time away from real work. Overall, I'm happy, and I'd like to grow in this career.

prompt: Do you prefer working from home or at the office? Why?
goals: use I prefer ... because
use a comparative adjective
finish with a conclusion
model: I prefer working from home, mainly because I save a lot of time. I don't have to spend two hours in traffic, so I have more energy. It's also quieter, which helps me concentrate. However, I think the office is better for team projects, because it's easier to talk face to face. In my opinion, the best option is a mix of both.

prompt: Have you ever used an AI tool? What did you use it for, and was it helpful?
goals: use the present perfect
use for or since with time
use the connectors but and so
model: Yes, I have. I've used an AI assistant for about a year. I mainly use it to improve my emails in English and to summarize long documents. It's very helpful because it saves time, but sometimes it makes mistakes, so I always check the answers. I haven't used it for creative work yet, but I'd like to try.

prompt: Describe the area where you live and say one thing you would like to improve.
goals: use there is / there are
use a comparative
use I would like + infinitive
useful: I would like the city to...
model: I live in a quiet neighborhood near the city center. There are many shops, a small park, and a good bakery nearby. It's safer than the area where I lived before. However, there aren't enough bike lanes, so cycling can be dangerous. I would like the city to build more lanes and plant more trees, because that would make the area healthier and nicer.

prompt: What would you do if your company changed its infrastructure completely?
goals: use a second conditional
use one connector: however / although
give a reason with because or since
model: If my company changed its infrastructure completely, I would first ask for a clear migration plan. Although change can be risky, it can also bring big advantages, such as lower costs and better performance. I'd start by learning the new tools, because I wouldn't want to slow down the team. The main advantage would be that we could work faster in the long run.

prompt: Describe a time you had to meet a tight deadline. How did you handle it?
goals: use the past simple and the past continuous
order actions with first / then / after that
use a contrast: although / however
model: Last year, I had to finish a report in two days. I was working on another project at the time, so I talked to my manager. First, I listed the most important tasks. Then I asked a colleague to help with the data. Although it was stressful, we finished on time. The experience taught me that asking for help early is better than trying to do everything alone.

prompt: What are the advantages and disadvantages of travelling alone?
goals: use for example to give examples
use contrast words: however / while
use comparatives with more than
model: Travelling alone has clear advantages. You can decide your own schedule, and you meet more people. However, it also has disadvantages. For example, it can feel lonely, and it's usually more expensive than traveling with others, because you don't share costs. Also, safety can be a concern in some places. While I enjoy my independence, I think the best option is to travel with one close friend.

prompt: How would you give bad news to a friend?
goals: use the second conditional
use wouldn't to say what to avoid
use a sequence: first / then / afterwards
useful: If I had to..., I would...
model: If I had to give bad news to a friend, I would do it in person, or at least by phone. I wouldn't send a text message, because it feels cold. First, I'd say something kind, and then I'd explain the situation clearly. I think it's important to be honest, but also to listen to how my friend feels. Afterwards, I'd offer to help in any way I could.

prompt: Do you think AI will change the way people learn languages?
goals: use will and might for predictions
give an example with for example
use a contrast: however / but
useful: I don't think it will replace...
model: I think AI will change language learning a lot. For example, students will be able to practice conversation at any time, and they'll get instant feedback on their mistakes. That might make learning faster and cheaper. However, I don't think it will replace teachers completely, because people still need motivation and human contact. In the future, I believe the best method will combine both.

prompt: Should students wear uniforms at school? Give your opinion.
goals: use first / second to organize arguments
use on the other hand
use as long as for a condition
model: In my opinion, school uniforms are a good idea. First, they make all students equal, so nobody feels bad about their clothes. Second, they save time in the morning, and parents don't have to spend as much money. On the other hand, uniforms can limit self-expression, which is important for teenagers. Overall, I'd support them, as long as students can choose some accessories.

prompt: Tell me about a movie, series or book that taught you something.
goals: use the past simple
use a relative clause with which or who
use for instance to give an example
model: One series that taught me something is a documentary about the oceans. It showed how plastic pollution, which affects millions of animals, is getting worse every year. I watched it with my family, and we changed some habits afterwards. For instance, we stopped using plastic bags and started buying in bulk. It made me realize that small actions really matter.

prompt: Describe a habit you would like to change and explain how you plan to change it.
goals: use used to for past habits
use going to for plans
show a result with so or as a result
model: I'd like to stop checking my phone before bed. I used to read the news for an hour, and as a result I slept badly. Now I'm going to leave the phone in another room and read a book instead. I've already tried it for a week, and I feel more rested. It isn't easy, but I'm sure it will be worth it.

prompt: What makes a good manager? Explain your ideas.
goals: use clear goals with a good manager + verb
add ideas with in addition / also
use instead of + -ing
model: A good manager listens first and speaks second. They give clear goals, so the team knows what's expected. They also trust people, instead of controlling every detail. In addition, a good manager gives honest feedback, even when it's difficult. I once had a boss who thanked us publicly and criticized us privately, and that made me work harder, because I felt respected.

prompt: Some companies are moving everything to the cloud. What are the risks and the benefits?
goals: use a concession with while or even though
use could or might for possibility
give a recommendation with should
model: Moving everything to the cloud offers clear benefits, such as scalability and lower upfront costs. Even though it sounds simple, it carries real risks. For instance, a company might become dependent on one provider, and a poorly configured service could expose sensitive data. In my view, organizations should migrate gradually, keep a recovery plan, and train their teams before making any irreversible decisions.

prompt: Should companies tell customers when they are talking to an AI?
goals: use should and must for obligation
use it depends on
contrast with whereas or on the other hand
model: I believe companies should tell customers when they're talking to an AI. People have a right to know, because it affects how much they trust the information. It also depends on the context. A simple booking bot might not need a long explanation, whereas a medical or financial service must always do so. Transparency builds trust in the long run, and hiding it could seriously damage a company's reputation.

prompt: Describe a project that went wrong and what you learned from it.
goals: use the third conditional
use the past perfect
reflect with in hindsight or looking back
useful: If we had..., we would have...
model: A few years ago, I worked on a project that went over budget. In hindsight, we hadn't defined the scope clearly, so the requirements kept changing. If we had agreed on priorities from the start, we would have finished on time. I learned to ask more questions early and to document decisions. Since then, I've always insisted on a short kickoff meeting before any work begins.

prompt: Is mass tourism doing more harm than good? Explain your view.
goals: use despite or in spite of
use a comparison with more ... than
conclude with all things considered
model: Mass tourism brings money and jobs, but I think it often does more harm than good. Despite the economic benefits, many residents can't afford to live in popular cities because of rising rents. Moreover, crowds damage historical sites and the environment. All things considered, destinations should limit visitor numbers and encourage people to travel in off-peak seasons, so the benefits are shared more fairly.

prompt: How do you handle a disagreement with a colleague or a friend?
goals: use softening phrases like I see your point, but
use a first conditional with if
use phrasal verbs: work out / sort out
model: When I disagree with someone, I try to stay calm and listen first. I usually say, "I see your point, but I look at it differently," and then I explain why. If the issue is serious, I suggest we talk in private so nobody feels embarrassed. Most of the time, we can work out a compromise. If we can't, I ask a neutral person to help us sort it out.

prompt: Is it better to be a specialist or a generalist in your career?
goals: contrast with whereas or while
hedge with tend to or arguably
state a clear position with a reason
model: Arguably, it depends on the stage of your career. Specialists tend to earn more in the short term because their skills are rare, whereas generalists adapt faster when the market changes. Personally, I'd recommend becoming a specialist in one area while keeping a broad understanding of others. That way, you're valuable now, and you don't get stuck if your field changes.

prompt: How has your culture changed in the last twenty years?
goals: use the present perfect
contrast used to with nowadays
link ideas with as a result
model: My country has changed a lot in the last twenty years. People used to buy everything in stores, but nowadays online shopping is normal. Families have also become smaller, and as a result, traditions like big Sunday lunches are less common. On the positive side, society has become more open to different lifestyles. It hasn't been an easy process, but I think most of the changes have been positive.

prompt: How has technology changed your daily life compared with ten years ago?
goals: use the present perfect
contrast used to with these days
use quantifiers: much more / far fewer
useful: Ten years ago, I used to...
model: Technology has transformed my daily life. Ten years ago, I used to carry cash and paper maps. These days, I pay with my phone and navigate with an app. I spend much more time online, and I've noticed that I read far fewer books. On the plus side, I stay in touch with family abroad every day, which wasn't so easy before.

prompt: What would make you trust a new app with your personal data?
goals: use the second conditional
use unless or as long as
use would and wouldn't for hypotheses
model: I would only trust a new app with my data if it were transparent about what it collects. I'd want clear privacy settings, and I wouldn't use it unless it offered two-step verification. A good reputation also matters, as long as it's backed by independent reviews. If an app asked for permissions it didn't need, I'd delete it immediately.

prompt: Could AI replace human creativity? Argue your position.
goals: use a complex concession: while it's true that...
hedge with arguably or to some extent
conclude with ultimately
model: While it's true that AI can produce impressive music and images, I don't believe it can replace human creativity. It recombines existing patterns, whereas people create from lived experience, emotion and context. To some extent, AI will change creative work, mainly by automating repetitive tasks. Ultimately, though, audiences value the story behind a work, and that human dimension is hard to replicate.

prompt: Is a four-day work week realistic for most companies?
goals: use provided that or as long as
use which means that
acknowledge a counterargument with admittedly
model: A four-day week can work for many companies, provided that productivity is measured by results rather than hours. Several trials have shown that employees are happier, which means that fewer people quit. Admittedly, it's harder for sectors like healthcare or customer support, which require constant coverage. Still, with careful planning and flexible schedules, I think more companies will adopt it within the next decade.

prompt: Is social media making us more connected or more isolated?
goals: use on the one hand ... on the other hand
use a passive: it has been shown that
show cause and effect with contribute to or lead to
model: On the one hand, social media lets us keep in touch with people across the world. On the other hand, it has been shown that heavy use can contribute to loneliness, because online contact often replaces real conversations. What matters is how we use it. If it leads to meeting in person, it connects us. If it only encourages comparison, it isolates us. So, in my view, the effect depends on our habits.

prompt: To what extent should a country protect its traditions in a globalized world?
goals: use to a certain extent
use a relative clause with which or whose
conclude with striking a balance
useful: The key is striking a balance...
model: To a certain extent, countries should protect their traditions, because they shape identity and give communities a sense of belonging. However, culture which doesn't evolve eventually loses relevance. Globalization also brings positive influences, such as new music and ideas. In my opinion, the key is striking a balance: preserving what is meaningful while remaining open to change.

prompt: If you could live abroad for five years, where would you go and what would worry you?
goals: use a second conditional
use would + infinitive for hypothetical worries
use as long as or provided that
useful: What would worry me most is...
model: If I could live abroad for five years, I would choose Portugal, since the culture is familiar and the language is similar. What would worry me most is being far from my family. If I had children, it would be even harder. However, I'd be happy to go as long as I could visit twice a year. I think living abroad would make me more independent.

prompt: Can long-distance friendships last? What does it take?
goals: use it takes + noun
use unless in a conditional sentence
use a concession: even though / however
model: Long-distance friendships can absolutely last, but it takes effort from both sides. Even though you can't meet often, regular calls, voice messages or shared activities help keep the connection alive. Unless both people make time, the relationship will fade. What matters most is being honest, so that neither feels forgotten. When you finally meet, it often feels as if no time has passed.

prompt: When software causes harm, who should be responsible: the developers, the company, or the users?
goals: use a passive: should be held accountable
contrast with whereas or nonetheless
hedge with it could be argued that
model: It could be argued that responsibility should be shared. Developers should be held accountable for negligent design, whereas companies must ensure proper testing and oversight. Users, nonetheless, also have a duty to follow instructions. However, when a company ignores known risks to save money, it should bear the greatest share. Clear regulation would help define who is responsible in each case.

prompt: Describe a decision that changed the course of your life.
goals: start reflecting with looking back
use the past perfect and a mixed conditional
use it turned out or what I didn't realize
useful: If I hadn't..., I would still...
model: Looking back, the decision to change careers was the most important one I've made. I had been working in finance for years, and I felt stuck. It turned out that moving into tech was the best thing I could have done. If I hadn't taken that risk, I would still be doing work that bored me. What I didn't realize then was how much I'd enjoy learning from scratch.

prompt: Should employers be allowed to monitor remote workers' computers?
goals: use should be allowed to
use a concession: although / even so
justify with on the grounds that
model: I don't think employers should be allowed to monitor everything on an employee's computer. Although companies have a legitimate interest in protecting data, constant surveillance damages trust. Even so, limited monitoring may be acceptable on the grounds that it's transparent and focused on security rather than productivity. Employees should always be informed about what is tracked. Trust, ultimately, produces better results than control.
